free_tier.stated: 3 GB per free personal account. Anaconda staff on the official forum: 'You'll hit a hard limit at 10 GB with the default storage settings. If you need a large amount of storage (>100GB), you'll need to contact sales.' Team plan is 50 GB.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

egress.terms: Free and unmetered for public packages. CDN-fronted (Cloudflare). conda-forge serves multi-GB packages anonymously with no auth.

tooling: anaconda-client (`anaconda upload`, `anaconda copy`, `anaconda remove`); REST at api.anaconda.org; conda itself is the client for download. Public channel listing is anonymous JSON.
chaining: Multiply by free orgs/accounts: 3 GB personal, 10 GB default cap, 50 GB Team. Even chained aggressively this is the smallest unit in the field — 10 TiB would need ~340 personal accounts at 3 GB. Not worth the operational cost against npm's 200 MB x unlimited.
limits_note: 3 GB personal free / 10 GB default hard limit / 50 GB Team. Per-package size not separately capped. Free accounts are public-only. Package versions can be removed but not edited.
